---
title: "Adding a new setup guide"
description: "The file structure and metadata to use when adding a step-by-step process to this site."
author: "Rito Ghosh"
date: "2026-10-15"
categories: [meta, quarto]
toc: true
---

This site keeps each setup process in its own directory. That makes it easy to keep screenshots, scripts, and downloadable files next to the guide that uses them.

## 1. Create a directory

Create a short, URL-friendly directory under `steps/`:

```bash
mkdir -p steps/my-new-guide
```

Use lowercase words separated by hyphens. Once a guide is published, avoid renaming its directory so existing links continue to work.

## 2. Add the guide

Create `steps/my-new-guide/index.qmd` with this front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "Set up the thing"
description: "What the reader will have working by the end."
author: "Rito Ghosh"
date: "2026-10-15"
categories: [tool-name, setup]
toc: true
---
```

Then write the process using numbered level-two headings:

```markdown
## 1. Install the dependency

Explain the step and show the command.

## 2. Configure the service

Explain the next step.

## 3. Verify the setup

Show how the reader can confirm that everything works.
```

## 3. Keep commands reproducible

Use fenced code blocks and name the language where possible:

````markdown
```bash
command --flag value
```
````

State where each command should run, call out values that must be replaced, and include the expected result after important steps.

## 4. Preview locally

From the repository root, run:

```bash
quarto preview
```

Quarto rebuilds the site as files change. Confirm that the guide appears on the home page, its category links work, and all commands and links are correct.

## 5. Publish

Commit the source files and push the `master` branch:

```bash
git add steps/my-new-guide

git commit -m "Add my new setup guide"

git push origin master
```

The GitHub Actions workflow renders the Quarto project and publishes it to GitHub Pages.
